problem_text:
A logistics manager must select packages to load onto a cargo truck. Available packages are:
* Package 1: volume 3 cubic meters, revenue $296
* Package 2: volume 1 cubic meter, revenue $267
* Package 3: volume 16 cubic meters, revenue $283
* Package 4: volume 38 cubic meters, revenue $197
* Package 5: volume 2 cubic meters, revenue $77
* Package 6: volume 6 cubic meters, revenue $278
* Package 7: volume 7 cubic meters, revenue $122
* Package 8: volume 45 cubic meters, revenue $94
* Package 9: volume 25 cubic meters, revenue $200
* Package 10: volume 14 cubic meters, revenue $46
* Package 11: volume 27 cubic meters, revenue $111
* Package 12: volume 46 cubic meters, revenue $83
* Package 13: volume 46 cubic meters, revenue $129
* Package 14: volume 31 cubic meters, revenue $220
* Package 15: volume 20 cubic meters, revenue $190
* Package 16: volume 11 cubic meters, revenue $151
* Package 17: volume 20 cubic meters, revenue $213
* Package 18: volume 24 cubic meters, revenue $132
* Package 19: volume 16 cubic meters, revenue $111
* Package 20: volume 27 cubic meters, revenue $80
* Package 21: volume 26 cubic meters, revenue $154
* Package 22: volume 49 cubic meters, revenue $115
* Package 23: volume 11 cubic meters, revenue $31
* Package 24: volume 21 cubic meters, revenue $184
* Package 25: volume 43 cubic meters, revenue $27
* Package 26: volume 19 cubic meters, revenue $106
* Package 27: volume 32 cubic meters, revenue $79
* Package 28: volume 42 cubic meters, revenue $33
* Package 29: volume 46 cubic meters, revenue $94

The truck has a maximum capacity of 499 cubic meters. Choose the package combination that maximizes total revenue without exceeding this volume limit. Each package is either fully loaded or not loaded at all.
